instructions: Four fresh first drafts from sources+latest profile/draftprompt, no access to their earlier synthetic drafts and no lintfeedback before saving. Existing agent retained broader task context. These are additional to the100, not a blind model benchmark.

lint.message: 'itself' - use sparingly; if it does not change the meaning, drop it
'I am' -> 'I'm'. The voice uses contractions. Skip only when the expanded form falls at the end of a sentence or carries deliberate emphasis.
'did not' -> 'didn't'. The voice uses contractions. Skip only when the expanded form falls at the end of a sentence or carries deliberate emphasis.

the opening sentence announces a count of items ('two things', 'three reasons') and the paragraph then lists them. That is a list. Fix: convert the items to a bullet list and drop the count - the bullets show it.

sentence has 4 commas (max 3). Fixes: (1) convert to a bullet list; (2) split into shorter sentences. Convert to a bullet list only when BOTH (a) each item is 3+ words and items are parallel in structure, AND (b) the author already signalled enumeration (colon + items, or 3+ adjacent sentences with the same opener). Skip conversion when items end in 'and others'/'and more'/'and so on', when commas are clausal (joining clauses, not items), or when inline reads fine.

sentence has 30 words and 2 commas, and the commas look like clause boundaries (subordinating conjunction, chain of actions, or mixed subjects). Fix: make ONE split at a natural clause boundary, usually into two sentences. Do NOT chop into many short fragments (that trips choppy-rhythm) and do NOT convert to bullets (that would break the meaning). Test: can you write a single lead-in line that all the commas finish without re-introducing the subject or verb? Yes -> bullet list. No -> split into 2-3 sentences.
'did not' -> 'didn't'. The voice uses contractions. Skip only when the expanded form falls at the end of a sentence or carries deliberate emphasis.

flat copular definition 'The second source is a...': it just equates the subject with a category and reads as dull and formal. Prefer active voice or lead with the thing itself: 'We use X', 'X does Y', or 'We will use `id`, a <description>'.
